cognitive_load_golden.json is generated from the Python resolver (resolve_cognitive_load) over synthetic, neutral inputs; each case records the scripted reader outputs, the queries the resolver issued with their parameters, and the result it returned.

Owner-only rule: eight cases hold the Go resolver's answer, not the Python resolver's. The Python resolver is deleted. When no ownership row resolved a candidate repository to the requested team, it read every team's repo_patterns and accepted a pattern match. The resolver now reads no repo_patterns: a repository with no team_repo_ownership row is owned by no team, the rule the metric families and the AI analytics team scope use. The eight cases are team_repo_pattern_fallback_exact, team_repo_pattern_fallback_glob, team_repo_pattern_more_specific_other_team, team_repo_pattern_no_match, team_repo_no_teams_at_all, team_repo_team_without_patterns, team_repo_two_candidates_first_native_other_second_pattern_this and team_repo_two_candidates_none_match. In each, the queries and parameters end at the ownership read, and the result is the empty result (total_days 0, no signals). Three of them (pattern_fallback_exact, pattern_fallback_glob, two_candidates_first_native_other_second_pattern_this) answered rows before. Their scripted inputs are unchanged. The other eighteen cases are byte-equal. The change was written by the script recorded in the PR, not typed.

Shared ownership statement (CHAOS-13685): fourteen cases hold the Go ownership read, not the Python one. The ownership read of the team and repository path renders the one ownership statement of the team scopes (teamscope.OwnershipFromWhere): an inactive team owns nothing, a row with an empty team id is skipped, and the rows are tested at one bound instant with the first recorded owners applied before the first record (package ownershipwindow), in place of now64(3). In each of the fourteen cases that issue the ownership read, the query keeps the reference projection, the candidate clause and the ORDER BY; its FROM ... WHERE is the token FROM team_repo_ownership {teamscope.OwnershipFromWhere}, which the golden test replaces by the rendered statement (pinned in package teamscope). Its parameters are candidate_ids, team_scope_org_id and team_scope_as_of (the golden instant, 2026-01-11 12:00:00.000) in place of org_id. Scripted inputs and results are unchanged: the scripted rows hold no inactive team, no empty team id and no row outside the window. The other twelve cases are byte-equal. The change was written by the script recorded in the PR, not typed.
